analysis:
Integration of both prior analyses plus the replayed source (changelog, hardware-support.md, prefix-cache.md, ssd-kv-cache.md, CapabilityCommandCheck.swift). No concrete security regression is supported by the visible evidence. The replayed units are documentation plus one test-check change (CapabilityCommandCheck.swift line ~185 now expects [.pipeline, .tensorParallel] for Gemma). The code behaviors in the prior analyses (fail-closed NativeWorkerRuntime routing, verified loader, sealed two-rank vote/confirm, tenant-scoped prefix tiers) are only partly verifiable from the replay. The omitted 319 units limit verification.

Docs state that Gemma TP prefixes are scoped by Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes into both the resident and SSD tiers, via the tenant partition (cacheSalt digest), with no scope when disabled. They also state that the SSD tier reuses QwenStagePrefixDiskTier (owner-only directories, TTL, daily write cap, native records) and that load agreement refuses a cache on/off mismatch between ranks. This matches T-041's posture (tenant scoping, TTL, HMAC) and is unchanged in kind, but it extends the at-rest and TTFT-oracle surface to Gemma TP. The same-account oracle remains the accepted SEC-035 risk.

Open questions for deeper review:
1. T-041 affected_files lists only provider-swift KVCacheSSD, not the cluster QwenStagePrefixDiskTier or the Gemma TP caller. The model likely needs an update to cover them.
2. I could not confirm in source that QwenStagePrefixDiskTier uses HMAC lookup tags under the KEK, the 30-minute TTL ceiling, or that ClusterWorkerPrefixCache.scope folds the tenant into both tiers.
3. Sealed all-sum authentication of the inter-Mac collectives (Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime) was not visible.
4. Cross-lane KV and cache isolation in multi-lane Gemma TP (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_BATCH_LANES) was not visible.
5. The mlx-swift-lm submodule bump is unreviewable here.
6. Availability: a non-Stopped error on one rank could stall the peer's confirm collective, but both ranks are authenticated and cooperating.
